summary.headline: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue rose 59.7% YoY to INR 1,169.2 crores as Punjab ramped up; management guides FY27 consolidated EBITDA north of INR 500 crores.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue grew 3% YoY to INR 752.8 crores with EBITDA up 16.9% to INR 82.5 crores and margin at 11%. Consolidated Q4 revenue of INR 1,169.2 crores and EBITDA of INR 94.4 crores (8.1% margin) reflect the first full quarters of Punjab Phase 1 ramp-up, which management says reached full capacity only at end-March 2026. Consolidated FY26 PAT was INR 77.3 crores, weighed down by higher depreciation and finance cost after Punjab capitalisation. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 5,600-5,700 crores and EBITDA north of INR 500 crores, with Phase 2 at Punjab targeted for end-FY27.

segments.name: Silvassa (standalone)
segments.commentary: Ran at about 95% utilisation across polyester, cotton and technical textile yarns through FY26; FY26 production 2.31 lakh MT and sales 2.28 lakh MT. Value addition above 40%. Management targets about INR 3,100 crores revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Punjab (subsidiary, Phase 1)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 ramp-up completed end-March 2026 after running a quarter late; Q4 utilisation guided at 80-85%. Targets about INR 2,600 crores revenue from Q2 FY27 and about 10% value addition currently. Products are tuned to North India coarser yarns.

segments.name: Technical textiles (Silvassa)
segments.commentary: Capacity doubling from 9,000 to 18,000 MT per annum; commissioning by end Q1 FY27, with about INR 150 crores of incremental revenue expected at peak.

segments.name: Cotton yarn (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh, PM MITRA)
segments.commentary: Adding 72,000 spindles; land of about 50 acres bought for about INR 26 crores, possession expected by end of calendar 2026. Expected revenue INR 400-450 crores, with production about 10-12 months after ground-breaking.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR 5,600-5,700 crores (Silvassa about INR 3,100 crores, Punjab about INR 2,600 crores).
FY27 consolidated EBITDA guided north of INR 500 crores; management aims for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin but calls its stance conservative given the global situation.
FY27 PBT guided at about INR 225-250 crores after interest and depreciation, per management's reading of the outlook.
Finance cost to stay north of INR 125 crores consolidated; debt repayments of INR 100-125 crores per year, with no big debt planned near term.
Peak consolidated revenue of INR 7,500-7,700 crores expected by end of FY28 after Phase 2 Punjab (about INR 4,000 crores), Silvassa (about INR 3,200 crores) and cotton yarn (about INR 400 crores).
Punjab Phase 2 targeted for commissioning by end FY27.
Solar power of 32 MW hybrid from Serentica, with a payback of about 3 years; negligible cost benefit in FY27, full benefit in FY28.
capex_capacity: Punjab Phase 1 ramp-up completed end-March 2026; Phase 2 equipment orders and an announcement are expected soon, with completion targeted by end FY27.
Silvassa technical yarn capacity doubling from 9,000 to 18,000 MT per annum, commissioning by end Q1 FY27.
Cotton yarn capacity of 72,000 spindles at Dhar, MP; ground work to start after the monsoon once MPIDC levels the land, expected in the last quarter of calendar 2026.
Gas-based heating at Silvassa; Punjab runs on agri-waste fuel and uses no gas.

Punjab PTA and MEG linked projects: about 2.5 million tonnes of PTA capacity (GAIL and Indian Oil) had not commissioned by the call; GAIL now expects supply from July and Indian Oil targets year-end start-up.
demand_pricing: Cotton yarn prices rose significantly in Q4 on sharp spot cotton increases and manufacturing disruption, with demand holding up; realisations on cotton only marginally higher YoY.
Management says polyester spreads were good before the West Asia war; crude-linked raw material increases were passed on after a lag, and downstream demand is back to base.
Punjab sells coarser yarns to North India; management denied offering discounts beyond a small freight-arbitrage share passed to customers.
Export share about 5% of Silvassa volume; consolidated export share expected to stay flat as Punjab exports are limited.
Gas costs at Silvassa up 50-60%, with gas about 6-7% of operating cost; this is a headwind at Silvassa only.
Import duty on PTA waived; management hopes the status quo remains but noted it is outside its control.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins at Sanathan Polycot (Punjab) lagging Silvassa?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Silvassa ran at full capacity through the war-related disruption, and Punjab ramp-up finished only in March after a one-quarter delay. Product line-up realignment is expected to show margin benefits from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory and payable days rise (payables from about 59 days in FY25 to about 104 days)?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Punjab ramp-up raised material and FG inventory, and about INR 180 crores of raw material was in transit. Punjab stock is lower than Silvassa, and days should fall as full-quarter COGS builds.

qa_highlights.question: Debt and interest cost: is FY26 gross debt the peak?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross debt of about INR 1,500 crores is the peak, with repayments of INR 100-125 crores a year. Average cost of debt is about 7.25% after including trade payables carrying LC interest beyond 68 days; finance cost stays above INR 125 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to the INR 7,000 crore-plus revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is INR 5,600-5,700 crores, and peak revenue of INR 7,500-7,700 crores is expected by end FY28 after Phase 2 and cotton yarn.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Punjab margin reach Silvassa levels and double-digit consolidated EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin, calls its guidance conservative given the global situation, and tracks performance on EBITDA per tonne rather than percentage.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Punjab Phase 1 utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 80-85% utilisation in the current quarter, with the facility aiming to run flat out like Silvassa over time.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to currency, raw materials and PTA supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Euro-denominated ECB is hedged for the full tenure, imports are booked on arrival, and the import and export balance limits raw material risk. PTA supply depends on GAIL and Indian Oil start-up timing.

risks_watch: Crude and cotton volatility: pass-through lags, and management said inventory was held back in some quarters when crude was expected to rise.
Punjab execution: utilisation of 80-85% in Q1 FY27, product realignment and the gap in gross margin versus Silvassa.
Phase 2 Punjab and cotton yarn timelines (end FY27 and 10-12 months after ground-breaking) and the still-unannounced equipment orders.
PTA supply delays from GAIL and Indian Oil and the duty waiver status.
Working capital: inventory and payable days elevated; management expects normalisation only over two to three quarters.
Management did not provide a segment split between cotton and technical textiles because it does not track them separately.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the FY27 ramp, but cautious on margins and macro: management called its double-digit margin target conservative and said the global situation remains fluid. Evasive on the next growth leg beyond Phase 2 and the cotton expansion, promising details later.
key_quotes: We are looking at north of INR 500 crores for the FY27 EBITDA margins.
Because we have ramped up only in the end of March to full capacity.
Nothing on the currency side really affects us because we have an ECB which is in Euros, but we have been hedged for the entire loan tenure of that ECB.
Sure. This is our peak gross debt level and we are expecting a payouts of close to INR 100 to INR 125 crores every year.

We aim to do that double-digit EBITDA. There's no doubt on that. But we are confident at this moment to say looking at the current global situation, we are a little conservative in stating what we aim to do.

growth.why: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR 5,600-5,700 crores (about 47% over FY26's 3,811 crores) and EBITDA north of INR 500 crores, mainly from Punjab Phase 1 full run-rate (about INR 2,600 crores) plus Silvassa at about INR 3,100 crores; backing is partly specific (Punjab Phase 1 completed, Silvassa tech yarn doubling by end Q1 FY27) but Phase 2 and Dhar lack firm orders or timelines beyond targe
